summary.one_liner: You learn the common data science team structures (decentralized, functional, consulting, centralized, Center of Excellence, federated, democratic) and the main data roles, from data analyst to data engineer.
keywords: type a vs type b data scientist
how to organize a data science team
embedding data scientists in business units
takeaways: Compare seven team structures (decentralized, functional, consulting, centralized, Center of Excellence, federated, democratic) and their drawbacks.
Learn how the roles of data analyst, business analyst, data scientist, ML engineer, data architect and data engineer differ.
Understand Michael Hochster's Type A (analysis) and Type B (building) data scientist distinction.
Choose a structure based on company size and analytics maturity, e.g. consulting for SMBs and CoE for enterprises with a data roadmap.
Apply practical tips such as hiring in-house talent first, embedding data scientists, and fostering cross-functional collaboration.
summary.summary: The article, from AltexSoft, explains how to organize a data science team as machine learning adoption grows. It describes the main roles (chief analytics officer, data analyst, business analyst, data scientist, ML engineer, data journalist, data architect, data engineer, and application/visualization engineer) along with their preferred skills. It then walks through seven team structures based on Accenture's classification, listing the implementation fit and pitfalls of each. It closes with hiring and integration recommendations and notes on common barriers to ML adoption.
